text:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle can be understood by comparing it to the challenge of navigating a crowded room with your eyes closed. In this analogy, attempting to precisely determine your location (position) by carefully avoiding contact with others makes it difficult to gauge the speed and direction of the people around you (momentum). Conversely, if you focus on sensing the flow and speed of the crowd, you lose precise awareness of your exact spot within it. This illustrates the fundamental trade-off in quantum mechanics: the more precisely one property of a particle is known, the less precisely the other can be determined.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
